n: In July 1830 the Lord speaks directly to Emma Smith, Joseph’s wife, calling her “my daughter.” All who receive the gospel become sons and daughters in God’s kingdom.

f.g: Emma Hale Smith married Joseph in 1827 and served as one of his early scribes during the translation.

f.w: sons and daughters in my kingdom

n: If Emma is faithful and virtuous, the Lord will preserve her life and give her an inheritance in Zion.
Her sins are forgiven, and she is called an “elect lady” — a chosen woman, a phrase from John’s second epistle. She later became the first president of the Relief Society in 1842.
Emma should not complain about not seeing the plates; they were withheld from her and the world for a wise purpose.

f.w: Murmur not because of the things which thou hast not seen

n: Her calling is to comfort Joseph in his trials with consoling, gentle words.
She is to travel with Joseph and act as his scribe when no one else is available, freeing Oliver for other assignments.
She will be set apart to explain scripture and encourage the Church as the Spirit directs.

f.g: in early Church usage, “ordained” could mean appointed or set apart to a calling, not necessarily priesthood office.

n: Joseph will lay hands on her to receive the Holy Ghost, and her time will be spent writing and learning.
Emma need not fear, for Joseph will support her; his calling is to the Church, to receive revelation for them.
Emma should set aside worldly things and seek something better — counsel that applies to every disciple.

f.w: lay aside the things of this world

n: Emma is to compile a selection of sacred hymns. Her hymnbook was published in 1835, and music has been central to Latter-day Saint worship ever since.

f.g: A Collection of Sacred Hymns, for the Church of the Latter Day Saints was printed in Kirtland in 1835.

n: A beloved verse: the Lord delights in heartfelt song, and the song of the righteous is a prayer he answers with blessings.

f.w: the song of the righteous is a prayer unto me

n: Lift up your heart, rejoice, and hold tight to your covenants.
Stay meek and avoid pride. Emma should take joy in her husband and the glory that will come to him.
Keep the commandments and receive a crown of righteousness; otherwise, one cannot come where the Lord is.

f.w: where I am you cannot come

n: The Lord declares that this counsel is his voice to everyone — not just Emma.

f.w: this is my voice unto all
